answer:
RESULT: analysis executed end-to-end on the Black NLS79 subsample (n=3,013; 159 ever-jailed). Headline pattern: the wealth gap between ever-jailed and never-jailed Black respondents over 1985–1996 widens monotonically with baseline 1985 wealth — the largest absolute jail-related wealth penalty falls on the highest-baseline-wealth Black respondents, not the lowest. The lowest tertile is pinned at $0 throughout; the middle and top tertiles show median collapse for the jailed (middle: $1,400 in 1985 → $0 in 1996 while never-jailed climbed $1,400 → $7,450; top: $11,150 → $4,700 while never-jailed grew $11,900 → $26,750). OLS on Δwealth_1996_1985 with ever_jailed × tertile + sex (Black, n=3,013) gives a top-tertile interaction of −$41,995 (p=0.18) raw and −$37,040 (p=0.012) under 1/99-percentile windorization — directional consistency, significance sensitive to upper-tail outliers. Submission deliverables below.

submission.answer (natural-language hypothesis):
"Among Black National Longitudinal Survey of Youth 1979 (NLS79) respondents, the wealth gap between those who were ever jailed during 1985–94 and those who were never jailed widened markedly between 1985 and 1996, and the size of that jail-related wealth gap — across the proxy for 'income level' supplied here (the within-Black tertile of 1985 composite wealth, because the supplied file has no income column) — increased monotonically with the respondent's baseline 1985 wealth. In absolute dollar terms, mean 1985→1996 wealth change by jail status was +$6,269 (jailed) vs +$23,752 (never-jailed) in the lowest 1985-wealth tertile, +$10,196 vs +$39,587 in the middle tertile, and a loss of −$4,248 vs a gain of +$54,760 in the highest tertile — i.e., the largest absolute jail wealth penalty fell on Black respondents who started out the richest in 1985. In median terms: in the middle tertile the never-jailed median climbed from $1,400 (1985) to $7,450 (1996) while the jailed median collapsed from $1,400 to $0; in the top tertile the never-jailed median grew from $11,900 to $26,750 while the jailed median fell from $11,150 to $4,700; the share of respondents with exactly zero wealth in 1996 was 19% (never-jailed) vs 41% (jailed) in the top tertile and 24% vs 59% in the middle tertile. An OLS regression of 1985→1996 wealth change on ever_jailed, baseline-wealth tertile (Black subsample), sex, and the ever_jailed × tertile interaction (n=3,013; all six tertile×jail cells had n ≥ 39, no collapse required) yields a negative interaction concentrated in the top tertile (jail × T3_high: −$41,995, p=0.18 raw; −$37,040, p=0.012 after 1/99-percentile windorization for outlier robustness); the joint interaction term is statistically marginal in raw data (F(2,3006)=0.89, p=0.41), so the cleaner statement is directional and monotone in the descriptive objects (mean change, median trajectory, zero-share), with regression-significance sensitive to extreme upper-tail wealth rather than to the sign or pattern.
¹Caveats. Descriptive, not causal — selection into incarceration, reverse causality, binary ever_jailed over 1985–94 with no duration/intensity/timing, no real income variable (proxy = within-Black 1985 composite wealth tertile), and the processed file is fully complete only on supplied columns (panel attrition has been absorbed upstream of this file). Schema drift: the file's race value 'hipanic' corresponds to the metadata's 'hispanic' and is treated as a typo."

payload.hypothesis: Among Black NLS79 respondents, ever having been jailed during 1985–94 is associated with substantially lower 1985→1996 wealth growth than never having been jailed, and the dollar size of that association widens monotonically across the within-Black tertiles of baseline 1985 wealth — the proxy used for "income level" given that the supplied file has no income column — with the largest absolute jail-related wealth penalty (mean Δ-wealth −$4,248 vs +$54,760; median 1996 wealth $4,700 vs $26,750) falling on the highest-baseline-wealth Black respondents, while in the lowest tertile median wealth is already pinned at $0 for both groups.
payload.workflow: Loaded data/nls_incarceration_processed.csv (12,013 × 6; zero missing). Restricted to race='black' (n=3,013; ever_jailed 0/1 = 2,854/159; male/female split within ever_jailed = 143/16). Computed within-Black tertiles of composite_wealth_1985 (cutpoints $0 and $3,830). Cross-tabulated tertile × ever_jailed: minimum cell n = 39, no collapse required (planned rule was cells ≥ 30). Reported within-cell medians (1985, 1990, 1996), zero-mass shares (1985, 1996), and means. Fit OLS Δwealth_1996_1985 ~ C(ever_jailed) * C(tertile_1985) + sex_male on the Black subsample; replicated with the same model on wealth windorized at the 1st/99th percentiles for robustness against extreme upper-tail observations. Wrote artifacts/analysis.py (executed), artifacts/cell_stats.csv, artifacts/ols_full_summary.txt, artifacts/ols_windorized_summary.txt.
